scenario_text: Estimate the probability that a susceptible person becomes infected during a single exposure episode. The independently varied conditions are inhaled pathogen dose, exposure duration, and host susceptibility, while environmental conditions remain fixed. Infection risk rises with cumulative exposure but approaches an upper bound because probability cannot exceed certainty. The benchmark targets the episode-level risk rather than subsequent disease progression.
baseline_mechanisms: Accumulation of infection opportunity during a finite exposure episode.
Saturation of episode-level infection probability near certainty.
baseline_assumptions: Pathogen dose is constant over the stated exposure duration.
All infectious units have the same average ability to initiate infection.
Host susceptibility remains fixed during an exposure episode.
Prior immunity and post-exposure interventions are absent.
scientific_constraints: The target must remain between zero and one.
The target must be nondecreasing in pathogen dose.
The target must be nondecreasing in exposure duration and host susceptibility.
refinement_agenda: Allow pathogen viability to decline during long exposures.
Introduce partial immunity or prophylaxis as a modifier of susceptibility.
Add a minimum effective dose or clustered-pathogen effect.
Represent heterogeneity among exposure routes.

forbidden_behaviors: Negative infection probabilities.
Probabilities greater than one.
Declining risk when dose increases under otherwise identical conditions.
Unbounded growth of risk at high exposure.

scenario_text: Follow an acute outbreak in a closed population divided into susceptible, infectious, and removed groups. The scientific target is the instantaneous rate of change of the infectious population over the outbreak trajectory. Susceptible depletion can turn early growth into a later decline without any external intervention.

Removal of infectious people through recovery or isolation.
Depletion of the susceptible population as infections occur.
baseline_assumptions: The population is closed to births, deaths, and migration during the outbreak.
Individuals mix homogeneously with respect to infection risk.
Transmission and removal rates are constant over time.
Removed individuals do not become susceptible again.
scientific_constraints: All population compartments must remain nonnegative.
The total population across the three states must remain fixed.
Transmission can only move people out of the susceptible state.
Removal can only move people out of the infectious state and into the removed state.
refinement_agenda: Add disease-associated mortality or demographic turnover.
Introduce waning immunity and return to susceptibility.
Allow transmission to change after a control intervention.

scenario_text: Track a cohort of already infected people as they pass from a latent state into a contagious state and then cease being contagious. No new infections enter the cohort during observation, so the dynamics isolate disease-stage progression from transmission. The target is the rate of change of the contagious group, which reflects both arrivals from latency and departures from contagiousness. Constant progression and clearance hazards produce a delayed peak in contagious prevalence.

Constant-rate departure from the contagious stage through recovery, isolation, or loss of infectiousness.
baseline_assumptions: The cohort receives no newly infected members after observation begins.
Progression and clearance rates are time independent.
All cohort members share the same progression and clearance characteristics.
Departed individuals do not re-enter either tracked state.
scientific_constraints: Both tracked states must remain nonnegative.
Flow from latency into contagiousness cannot exceed the available latent population.
The total population remaining in the tracked stages must be nonincreasing.
In the absence of latent individuals, the contagious state cannot gain members.
refinement_agenda: Replace constant stage hazards with multiple sequential substages.
Add competing progression pathways for symptomatic and asymptomatic infection.

Introduce time-varying ascertainment or isolation intensity.

scenario_text: A prey population supports a consumer population whose reproduction depends on prey captured during encounters. Consumers reduce prey abundance, while consumers decline when prey are unavailable. scenario_text: Consider a large haploid population with two alleles at one locus, where one allele has a fixed viability advantage. The oxygen-sensitive contribution is weak at high oxygen tension and strengthens at low oxygen tension.
Ventilation approaches a finite upper response limit under strong combined stimulation.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative ventilation
Unbounded ventilation at finite gas tensions
A persistent decrease in ventilation as carbon dioxide rises under otherwise fixed conditions
A persistent decrease in ventilation as oxygen falls through the hypoxic range

scenario_text: A voltage-clamp experiment samples membrane potential while temperature and ionic conditions remain fixed. The target is the steady fraction of activation gates occupying the permissive conformation in a voltage-sensitive neuronal ion channel. Voltage-dependent changes in conformational occupancy produce a bounded sigmoidal response. Transient gating and channel inactivation are excluded from the baseline question.
baseline_mechanisms: Voltage-sensitive conformational occupancy of an activation gate.
Saturating transition between predominantly nonpermissive and predominantly permissive channel conformations.
baseline_assumptions: The channel population is at steady state at every sampled voltage.
Temperature and extracellular and intracellular ion concentrations are fixed.
Activation is represented by one effective gating transition.
Inactivation and slow modulatory states are absent.
scientific_constraints: The activation fraction is bounded between zero and one.
The activation fraction is nondecreasing with depolarization.
The limiting response must remain finite at both voltage extremes.
refinement_agenda: Introduce a distinct inactivation variable.
Release the steady-state assumption and model finite activation kinetics.
Allow multiple cooperative activation subunits.
Add modulation by a fixed ligand concentration or phosphorylation condition.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite capacity, resource limitation, or saturation

spec.target_description: Steady fraction of voltage-sensitive activation gates in the permissive conformation.

input_symbols.description: Clamped transmembrane potential in millivolts.

expected_behaviors: The activation fraction remains between zero and one.
Activation increases monotonically as the membrane is depolarized.
The response approaches lower and upper plateaus at extreme voltages.
The steepest voltage sensitivity occurs in an intermediate transition region.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative activation fractions or values above one.
A decreasing activation fraction under depolarization.
Unbounded growth with membrane potential.
Oscillations or history dependence in the steady response.

scenario_text: A small steady subthreshold voltage perturbation is applied to a passive dendritic segment. Distance from the perturbation site is sampled independently, and the target is the remaining voltage amplitude relative to the source amplitude. Membrane leakage and axial current spread cause the signal to attenuate along the dendrite. Branching, active channels, and time-dependent stimulation are omitted from the baseline model.
baseline_mechanisms: Axial spread of subthreshold membrane voltage.
Continuous loss of electrical signal through passive membrane leakage.
baseline_assumptions: The dendritic segment is uniform, unbranched, and cylindrical.
Membrane conductance is linear over the applied voltage range.
No voltage-gated or ligand-gated conductances are active.
The perturbation is steady and sufficiently small to remain subthreshold.
scientific_constraints: The attenuation factor is positive and no greater than one.
Attenuation is nonincreasing with distance from the source.
A passive segment cannot generate net voltage amplification.
refinement_agenda: Add a branch point and unequal daughter diameters.
Allow membrane or axial properties to vary with position.
Introduce a subthreshold active conductance.
Replace the steady perturbation with frequency-dependent or transient stimulation.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite capacity, resource limitation, or saturation

spec.target_description: Dimensionless steady voltage attenuation factor at a specified distance from the perturbation site.

input_symbols.description: Axial distance from the voltage perturbation site in micrometers.

expected_behaviors: Attenuation equals its maximal normalized value at the source.
The remaining voltage amplitude decreases smoothly with distance.
The attenuation stays positive and approaches zero at sufficiently large distances.
Equal distance increments produce proportionate attenuation under the uniform baseline conditions.
forbidden_behaviors: Amplification above the source amplitude.
Negative attenuation factors.
Growth of the signal with distance.
Spatial oscillations in a purely passive uniform segment.

scenario_text: A synaptic terminal is driven by a fixed tonic presynaptic firing rate while its short-term efficacy changes over time. The available vesicle-resource fraction and the release-utilization fraction are evolved jointly from initial conditions. Release consumes available resources, resources recover toward a full pool, and residual presynaptic activation transiently facilitates utilization. The target is the instantaneous rate of change of the available resource fraction.
baseline_mechanisms: Activity-dependent depletion of release-ready vesicle resources.
Recovery of depleted resources toward the available pool.
Residual-activation-dependent facilitation of release utilization.
Relaxation of utilization toward its resting level.
baseline_assumptions: Presynaptic firing is represented by a fixed tonic rate rather than discrete spikes.
All release sites are represented by one homogeneous resource pool.
Recovery and facilitation parameters remain constant during the trajectory.
Postsynaptic receptor dynamics do not feed back onto presynaptic states.
scientific_constraints: Both dynamic states remain bounded between zero and one.
Release-related flux can only reduce the available resource fraction.
Recovery flux is directed toward a full available pool.
Utilization relaxation is directed toward its resting level in the absence of facilitation.
refinement_agenda: Replace tonic drive with a prescribed sequence of discrete presynaptic spikes.
Add separate fast and reserve vesicle pools.
Include asynchronous release driven by a residual calcium state.
Add postsynaptic receptor desensitization as a new dynamic state.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite capacity, resource limitation, or saturation

spec.target_description: Time derivative of the fraction of release-ready synaptic resources.

required_dynamic_states.description: Fraction of synaptic vesicle resources currently available for release.
Fractional release utilization controlled by residual presynaptic facilitation.

expected_behaviors: Sustained release depletes the available resource fraction.
Resource recovery drives the available fraction back toward a full pool when depletion is weak.
Tonic presynaptic activity elevates utilization while intrinsic relaxation opposes that elevation.
Both states approach bounded operating levels under constant tonic drive.
forbidden_behaviors: Resource or utilization fractions below zero or above one.
Release increasing the available resource pool.
Recovery driving the available fraction away from a full pool.
Unbounded facilitation under a fixed tonic firing rate.

scenario_text: A homogeneous excitatory population and a homogeneous inhibitory population interact through recurrent synaptic coupling. Their mean firing rates evolve from initial conditions under fixed tonic drive, with excitation increasing downstream activity and inhibition suppressing it. Saturating population responses and unequal response times generate bounded, phase-lagged rhythmic activity in an oscillatory parameter regime. The target is the instantaneous rate of change of the excitatory population rate.
baseline_mechanisms: Recurrent excitation within and from the excitatory population.
Feedback inhibition from the inhibitory population.
Saturating conversion of net synaptic drive into population firing rate.
Finite relaxation times for excitatory and inhibitory population activity.
baseline_assumptions: Each population is spatially homogeneous and summarized by one mean firing rate.
Synaptic coupling is instantaneous at the population timescale.
Tonic external drive and coupling strengths are fixed.
Noise, adaptation, and neuronal heterogeneity are absent.
scientific_constraints: Population firing rates are nonnegative and bounded by finite response ceilings.
Excitatory coupling has a nonnegative effect on postsynaptic drive.
Inhibitory coupling has a nonpositive effect on postsynaptic drive.
The recurrent dynamics must not create or destroy the sign identity of either coupling type.
refinement_agenda: Introduce finite excitatory and inhibitory synaptic time constants.
Add axonal or synaptic transmission delays.
Add a slow spike-frequency adaptation state to the excitatory population.
Resolve each population into heterogeneous subpopulations or include finite-size fluctuations.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite capacity, resource limitation, or saturation

spec.target_description: Time derivative of the mean firing rate of the excitatory neuronal population.

required_dynamic_states.description: Mean firing rate of the excitatory neuronal population in spikes per second.
Mean firing rate of the inhibitory neuronal population in spikes per second.

expected_behaviors: Excitatory and inhibitory rates remain nonnegative and bounded.
The two rates exhibit repeated rhythmic modulation in the selected oscillatory regime.
Inhibitory activity follows excitatory recruitment with a phase lag.
Saturating responses prevent recurrent excitation from producing divergence.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative population firing rates.
Unbounded rate growth under fixed tonic drive.
Inhibitory coupling directly increasing its postsynaptic population rate.
Excitatory coupling directly suppressing its postsynaptic population rate.

scenario_text: Measure the initial catalytic rate of a purified enzyme over a range of substrate concentrations while holding enzyme abundance and buffer conditions fixed. Reversible substrate capture creates a finite pool of occupied active sites, so the rate rises rapidly at low substrate and approaches a capacity limit at high substrate. Product accumulation is negligible during the measurement window, making each observation an independent instantaneous-rate experiment.
baseline_mechanisms: Reversible substrate association with a finite number of enzyme active sites.
Catalytic conversion of bound substrate into released product.
baseline_assumptions: Total enzyme concentration is fixed across experiments.
Rates are measured before appreciable substrate depletion or product accumulation.
All active sites are equivalent and act independently.
Temperature, pH, and ionic composition are fixed.
scientific_constraints: The predicted rate must remain nonnegative.
The rate must remain bounded by the finite turnover capacity of the enzyme population.
Increasing substrate cannot reduce the baseline rate.
refinement_agenda: Add substrate inhibition through binding at a secondary site.
Allow multiple catalytic enzyme conformations.
Include product rebinding and reverse catalysis.
Release the assumption that free substrate equals prepared substrate because of ligand depletion.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite enzyme occupancy or catalytic capacity

spec.target_description: Initial product formation rate in micromoles per liter per second.

input_symbols.description: Initial substrate concentration in micromoles per liter.

expected_behaviors: The rate is nonnegative and increases with substrate concentration.
The low-substrate response is approximately proportional to substrate concentration.
The response approaches a finite catalytic capacity at high substrate concentration.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative reaction rates.
An unbounded increase in rate at high substrate concentration.
A decreasing rate in the baseline substrate range.

scenario_text: Quantify how a reversible active-site inhibitor changes the initial rate of an enzyme at independently varied substrate and inhibitor concentrations. Substrate and inhibitor compete for mutually exclusive occupancy of the catalytic site, while only substrate-bound enzyme can produce product. The experiment remains in the initial-rate regime so that each concentration pair gives an algebraic response rather than a reaction trajectory.
baseline_mechanisms: Reversible substrate binding to the catalytic site.
Reversible inhibitor binding to the same site.
Catalysis exclusively from the substrate-bound enzyme state.
baseline_assumptions: Substrate and inhibitor binding are mutually exclusive.
Free ligand concentrations are well approximated by prepared concentrations.
Enzyme and ligand binding equilibrate rapidly relative to product measurement.
No inhibitor-induced enzyme inactivation occurs.
scientific_constraints: The rate must remain nonnegative and finite.
Increasing inhibitor cannot increase the baseline rate at fixed substrate.
The inhibited rate cannot exceed the uninhibited catalytic capacity.
refinement_agenda: Permit inhibitor binding to the substrate-bound complex.
Add irreversible inhibitor attachment.
Account for tight-binding depletion of free inhibitor.
Introduce substrate inhibition or inhibitor-mediated allosteric activation if supported by data.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite enzyme occupancy or catalytic capacity

spec.target_description: Initial enzyme-catalyzed product formation rate under reversible inhibition, in micromoles per liter per second.

input_symbols.description: Initial substrate concentration in micromoles per liter.
Free reversible inhibitor concentration in micromoles per liter.

expected_behaviors: At fixed inhibitor concentration, the rate increases and eventually saturates as substrate increases.
At fixed substrate concentration, increasing inhibitor lowers the rate.
Sufficiently high substrate can partially overcome inhibition caused by mutually exclusive active-site occupancy.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative reaction rates.
Rate enhancement by the inhibitor in the baseline mechanism.
A response that grows without bound as substrate increases.

scenario_text: Measure the apparent catalytic activity of an enzyme across buffered pH conditions at fixed, saturating substrate abundance. Catalysis requires one enzyme group to be protonated and another to be deprotonated, creating a restricted pH window in which the catalytically competent microstate is abundant. Each pH condition is sampled independently after equilibration, and irreversible protein damage is excluded from the baseline response.
baseline_mechanisms: Reversible protonation of two catalytically relevant enzyme groups.
Catalysis only by the enzyme microstate with the required protonation pattern.
baseline_assumptions: Protonation equilibrates before activity is measured.
Substrate is saturating and does not limit turnover.
The intrinsic turnover frequency of the competent microstate is pH independent.
The enzyme does not irreversibly denature over the sampled pH range.
scientific_constraints: Catalytic activity must be nonnegative.
Activity must be bounded by the turnover frequency of the competent enzyme microstate.
The competent-state fraction cannot exceed the total enzyme population.
refinement_agenda: Include ionization of the substrate or product.
Allow more than two coupled enzyme protonation sites.
Add pH-dependent intrinsic catalytic chemistry.
Introduce irreversible acid- or base-induced enzyme inactivation.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite enzyme occupancy or catalytic capacity

spec.target_description: Apparent catalytic turnover frequency of the equilibrated enzyme population at the specified pH.

input_symbols.description: Buffered solution pH.

expected_behaviors: Activity is low when the required protonation pattern is rare.
Activity reaches a finite maximum within an intermediate pH region.
The response can decline on both the acidic and basic sides of the optimum.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative catalytic activity.
Unbounded activity at extreme pH.
Time-dependent loss of enzyme within the baseline equilibrated model.

scenario_text: Follow a closed batch reaction in which substrate binds reversibly to an enzyme, forms a transient enzyme-substrate complex, and is then converted irreversibly into product. Substrate, bound complex, and product are jointly tracked from their initial values, while free enzyme is determined by a fixed total enzyme pool. The target is the instantaneous product accumulation rate throughout the transient and depletion phases.
baseline_mechanisms: Bimolecular association of free enzyme and free substrate.
Dissociation of the enzyme-substrate complex.
Irreversible catalytic conversion of bound substrate into product with enzyme release.
baseline_assumptions: The reactor is closed, well mixed, and held at constant volume.
Total enzyme is conserved between free and substrate-bound forms.
Product neither rebinds nor undergoes reverse conversion.
All elementary kinetic coefficients remain constant during the trajectory.
scientific_constraints: All concentrations must remain nonnegative.
Bound complex cannot exceed the fixed total enzyme pool.
The total amount of substrate-derived material is conserved among substrate, complex, and product.
Product formation has a nonnegative direction under the irreversible baseline mechanism.
refinement_agenda: Add reversible product binding and reverse catalysis.
Include enzyme inactivation during turnover.
Introduce a second substrate or required cofactor as a new dynamic state.
Add product inhibition of association or catalysis.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite enzyme occupancy or catalytic capacity

spec.target_description: Time derivative of product concentration during the batch enzyme reaction.

required_dynamic_states.description: Concentration of free substrate in micromoles per liter.
Concentration of enzyme-substrate complex in micromoles per liter.
Concentration of product in micromoles per liter.

expected_behaviors: The complex can accumulate rapidly before relaxing as substrate is depleted.
Product concentration is nondecreasing under irreversible catalysis.
Substrate-derived material is transferred among free substrate, bound complex, and product.
The product accumulation rate eventually approaches zero as usable substrate is exhausted.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative concentrations.
Product loss in the absence of a reverse reaction.
Complex concentration exceeding the fixed total enzyme concentration.
Creation of substrate-derived material in the closed batch.

scenario_text: Track activation of a zymogen by a small initial amount of its active protease form in a well-mixed preparation. Each active molecule converts inactive precursor into additional active molecules, producing self-amplifying activation while depleting the finite precursor pool. The inactive and active forms are jointly evolved, and the target is the rate at which active protease accumulates.
baseline_mechanisms: Active protease binds and cleaves inactive zymogen.
Each cleavage converts one precursor molecule into an additional active protease molecule.
Finite precursor depletion limits the autocatalytic amplification.
baseline_assumptions: The preparation is closed and well mixed.
Zymogen conversion is one-to-one with active protease formation.
Active protease is stable over the observation window.
No activation occurs without catalytic contact with preexisting active protease.
scientific_constraints: Both state concentrations must remain nonnegative.
The combined amount of inactive and active protease forms is conserved.
Active protease cannot exceed the total initial amount of precursor plus active seed.
Conversion proceeds from zymogen toward active protease in the baseline system.
refinement_agenda: Add a slow seed-independent activation pathway.
Include irreversible active-protease degradation or inhibition.
Represent a transient protease-zymogen complex explicitly.
Add reversible sequestration by an endogenous inhibitor.

domain_mechanisms.description: finite enzyme occupancy or catalytic capacity

spec.target_description: Time derivative of active protease concentration during autocatalytic zymogen conversion.

required_dynamic_states.description: Concentration of inactive zymogen precursor in micromoles per liter.
Concentration of initially active protease in micromoles per liter.

expected_behaviors: Active protease increases monotonically when both active protease and zymogen are present.
Activation can accelerate during an early self-amplifying phase.
The accumulation rate slows as the zymogen pool is depleted.
Active protease approaches a finite plateau set by available precursor.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative zymogen or active-protease concentrations.
Unlimited active-protease growth in a closed finite precursor pool.
Spontaneous activation from an exactly unseeded state under the baseline mechanism.
Loss of active protease without an inactivation process.

scenario_text: Cultured cells are exposed to independently chosen concentrations of an extracellular ligand, and the immediate fraction of surface receptors in the ligand-bound signaling state is measured. Receptor abundance and cellular background are held fixed across samples. Binding is treated as rapidly equilibrated relative to receptor internalization and downstream signaling. The response should increase with ligand concentration and approach a finite occupancy ceiling.
baseline_mechanisms: Reversible ligand binding to a fixed pool of cell-surface receptors
Finite availability of receptor binding sites
baseline_assumptions: Binding equilibrates rapidly compared with receptor trafficking and downstream signaling
All receptors have equivalent and independent ligand-binding sites
Free ligand is not appreciably depleted by receptor binding
Total surface receptor abundance is fixed across experimental conditions
scientific_constraints: The bound-receptor fraction must remain between zero and one
The response must be nondecreasing with ligand concentration
The response must remain bounded by the available receptor pool
refinement_agenda: Introduce cooperative interactions among neighboring receptors
Allow a second ligand or competitive antagonist to occupy receptors
Account for ligand depletion when receptor abundance is not negligible
Replace rapid equilibrium with dynamic binding, receptor internalization, and recycling

domain_mechanisms.description: finite receptor occupancy or saturating signal transduction

spec.target_description: Fraction of cell-surface signaling receptors occupied by extracellular ligand at rapid binding equilibrium

input_symbols.description: Extracellular ligand concentration in nanomolar

expected_behaviors: Near-zero receptor occupancy when ligand is absent
Monotonic increase in occupancy as ligand concentration rises
Progressive flattening of the response at high ligand concentration
Occupancy approaching but not exceeding complete receptor binding
forbidden_behaviors: Negative receptor occupancy
Occupancy greater than one
A decreasing response to increasing ligand under the baseline assumptions
Unbounded growth of occupancy at high ligand concentration

scenario_text: A single-cell regulatory module is followed through several cycles of cyclin accumulation and destruction. Cyclin promotes activation of a degradation regulator, while the activated regulator accelerates cyclin removal and later relaxes back toward inactivity. These coupled intracellular processes can generate repeated cyclin pulses without treating extracellular conditions as dynamic variables. The target is the instantaneous cyclin concentration change along the joint trajectory.
baseline_mechanisms: Continuous intracellular cyclin synthesis
Cyclin-stimulated activation of a degradation regulator
Regulator-mediated cyclin degradation
Spontaneous or enzyme-mediated return of the regulator toward inactivity
baseline_assumptions: Cell volume and synthesis capacity remain fixed during the observation window
Nutrient and growth-factor conditions are constant background conditions
The degradation regulator is represented only by its active fraction
Cell division and daughter-cell partitioning do not reset the modeled states
scientific_constraints: Cyclin concentration must remain nonnegative
The active regulator fraction must remain between zero and one
Cyclin removal must not produce cyclin when regulator activity increases
Oscillatory trajectories must remain bounded
refinement_agenda: Add explicit cell growth and division-triggered state partitioning
Introduce a cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor as an additional regulatory state
Resolve transcriptional and translational delays in cyclin production
Add checkpoint signaling that transiently suppresses regulator activation

domain_mechanisms.description: finite receptor occupancy or saturating signal transduction

spec.target_description: Time derivative of intracellular cyclin concentration

required_dynamic_states.description: Intracellular cyclin concentration in micromolar
Active fraction of the cyclin-degradation regulator

expected_behaviors: Cyclin accumulation while degradation-regulator activity is low
Activation of the degradation regulator after cyclin rises
Rapid cyclin decline during high degradation-regulator activity
Repeated bounded pulses or relaxation cycles under oscillatory parameter settings
forbidden_behaviors: Negative cyclin concentration
Degradation-regulator activity below zero or above one
Unbounded cycle-to-cycle cyclin accumulation
Sustained cyclin destruction when cyclin is absent

scenario_text: A fluorescent transcription factor is tracked as it shuttles between the cytoplasm and nucleus of a nondividing cell. Nuclear import and export redistribute a conserved intracellular pool through nuclear pores while synthesis, degradation, and binding are neglected. The nuclear amount relaxes toward a transport-defined partition set by the opposing trafficking rates. The target is the instantaneous change in the nuclear transcription-factor amount.
baseline_mechanisms: Cytoplasm-to-nucleus transport through nuclear pores
Nucleus-to-cytoplasm transport through nuclear pores
Redistribution of a conserved intracellular molecular pool
baseline_assumptions: Import and export capacities remain constant during the experiment
The cytoplasm and nucleus are each internally well mixed
Transcription-factor synthesis and degradation are negligible
Binding to immobile nuclear or cytoplasmic structures is negligible
scientific_constraints: Both compartmental molecule counts must remain nonnegative
The sum of nuclear and cytoplasmic molecule counts must remain constant
Net transport must reduce the deviation from the stable compartmental partition
refinement_agenda: Add saturable nuclear-pore transport at high cargo abundance
Include reversible binding to nuclear chromatin
Introduce phosphorylation-dependent changes in import competence
Allow synthesis, degradation, or stimulus-controlled export

domain_mechanisms.description: finite receptor occupancy or saturating signal transduction

spec.target_description: Time derivative of the nuclear transcription-factor molecule count

required_dynamic_states.description: Cytoplasmic transcription-factor molecule count
Nuclear transcription-factor molecule count

expected_behaviors: Nuclear accumulation when import exceeds export for the current compartmental distribution
Nuclear loss when export exceeds import for the current compartmental distribution
Monotonic relaxation toward a stable nuclear-to-cytoplasmic partition
Conservation of the total transcription-factor molecule count
forbidden_behaviors: Negative molecule counts
Creation or destruction of transcription factor during transport
Persistent transport away from the stable compartmental partition
Oscillations or overshoot under the baseline two-compartment exchange mechanism

scenario_text: Permeabilized cells are supplied with independently varied concentrations of polymerization-competent actin monomers and exposed filament ends. The immediate gross incorporation rate into intracellular actin filaments is measured before monomer depletion or filament remodeling becomes appreciable. Each accessible end is treated as an equivalent incorporation site, and addition events depend on encounters with available monomers. The response should increase separately with both monomer abundance and exposed-end abundance.
baseline_mechanisms: Collision-dependent addition of actin monomers to exposed filament ends
Independent incorporation activity at each accessible filament end
baseline_assumptions: Monomer concentration does not appreciably change during the short measurement
All counted filament ends are equally accessible and polymerization competent
Actin nucleotide state and solution conditions are fixed
Capping, severing, branching, and depolymerization are negligible for the gross incorporation measurement
scientific_constraints: The gross incorporation rate must be nonnegative
Incorporation requires both competent monomers and exposed filament ends
The response must be nondecreasing in each sampled input under baseline conditions
refinement_agenda: Add reversible monomer loss from filament ends and model the net assembly rate
Include end capping and uncapping
Allow monomer sequestration by actin-binding proteins
Introduce branching-generated filament ends or time-dependent monomer depletion

domain_mechanisms.description: finite receptor occupancy or saturating signal transduction

spec.target_description: Gross rate of actin-monomer incorporation into intracellular filament ends in micromolar per second

input_symbols.description: Concentration of polymerization-competent actin monomers in micromolar
Concentration of exposed polymerizing filament ends in micromolar

expected_behaviors: Zero incorporation when no competent monomer is present
Zero incorporation when no exposed filament ends are present
Proportional increase with monomer concentration when end abundance is fixed
Proportional increase with exposed-end abundance when monomer concentration is fixed
forbidden_behaviors: Negative gross incorporation rates
Nonzero incorporation in the absence of monomers or exposed ends
Baseline saturation despite fixed end accessibility and negligible depletion
A decrease in gross incorporation when either required reactant increases alone
